answers.explanation: It's usually small, but nothing bounds it.
Head-of-line blocking, in the replication log.
Single-threaded apply can't keep up with parallel writes.
Log sequence numbers. MySQL uses GTIDs; MongoDB uses oplog timestamps.
Writes behind and seconds behind measure different things.
Naive metrics make an idle, caught-up follower look stale.
Checking only whether a follower is up isn't enough.
